role: the security engineer who has watched a host fall
verdict: The spec meets this lens where romeu parses the three agent inputs it names (memory, git objects, spool) and fails it everywhere else agent bytes or agent code cross out of the sandbox: julieta's own output, the kit builder, the release job and the maintainer's host loop are unnamed paths, and the one widening (ADR 0008) is written down with a compensating control that is a human memory and triggers that nothing produces.

findings.defect: The row 'Agent output that reaches the host' lists memory files, git objects and spool files, and omits julieta's --json stdout read over sbx env exec (version, setup, status, salvage), kit args from the spec, snapshot/heads.json and the TOML lock files, so no grammar, cap or validation is specified, fuzzed (10 10.1) or probed (A3 cannot replace the read-only binary) for them.
findings.scenario: The agent is root in the sandbox (05 5.4) and makes julieta status --json return a 400 MiB document, or a SHA field that is not hex, or a branch name with a path separator; romeu pull compares heads from it and romeu status prints it; nothing in the text bounds the read, the decode or the use of a string from it as a ref or a path.
findings.change: Add to 01 1.2 one table of every agent-influenced byte stream romeu reads, with columns bytes, parser, grammar, size cap, use and rejection outcome; add to 04 4.1 Output a rule that every document romeu decodes from a subprocess or a mount is decoded strictly, capped, and that no string from it becomes a path, a ref or an argv element without the 03 3.1 validators; add the decoders to the fuzz list of 10 10.1 and a hostile-output row to the hybrid level.
findings.cost: one table and two rules in the text; one invariant with its tagged test; a hybrid test with a fake julieta behind the fake sbx

findings.defect: The Build row says 'sbx builds them at create' and the spec never says where the build runs, what the builder can reach, or where a kit's lifecycle hooks execute, although a personal kit's install steps and hooks are agent-authored code from the config commit and 00 0.1 promises that nothing an agent wrote is executed on the host.
findings.scenario: A personal kit with a five-line install step passes the gate diff; sbx builds it in a BuildKit on the Docker engine side rather than inside the sandbox microVM, with the install-phase network and whatever the builder mounts; the step runs with that reach, and the operator believed 00 0.1 covered it because no row said otherwise.
findings.change: Add a boundary row to 01 1.3 for 'config repo -> kit builder' naming where sbx builds local kits and what the builder reaches; state in 06 6.1 where lifecycle hooks of a kit run and whether they are host commands under sbx's prompt; add to A11 and A14 (11 11.1) observations of the build host, the reachable network and the visible filesystem from an install step; add a 05 5.4 row for the residual.
findings.cost: one boundary row, two sentences, three probe observations, one residual-risk row; the decision whether personal kits may carry lifecycle hooks at all

findings.defect: The ask-first list omits every host-side parser of agent bytes and every builder of host commands: internal/memstore, internal/handoff, internal/salvage, internal/oci, internal/render, internal/sbxdrv, internal/shquote, internal/egress and e2e/fakesbx (which enforces I4 and I25 in tests), while I24's completeness rests on [review] and 12 12.4 says the approval line is typed by the author.
findings.scenario: A pull request changes a memstore reader to follow one symlink 'for the import case', touches no listed glob, needs no approval line, is merged by the sandbox's token (ADR 0008); the next romeu sync follows a planted symlink out of a memory dir.
findings.change: Add surfaces 'readers' (memstore, handoff, salvage, oci, the materialization code of render) and 'drivers' (sbxdrv, shquote, egress, e2e/fakesbx) to .github/ask-first.yaml in 05 5.3, and state in 05 5.3 what holds the ask-first surfaces today given 05 5.4 (the approval line plus the security log), so the list's worth is read where it is defined. The plan's question 28 already asks for three of these packages.
findings.cost: two entries in one YAML file and one sentence; more PRs carry an approval line

findings.defect: The row 'narrowing the sandbox's GitHub token' is the acceptance of the widest decision in the project, and its reopen triggers have no deterministic producer: 'every 2 autonomous work sessions' is counted by nobody (13 13.2 says v1 records no session start or end), 'an agent action nobody asked for' depends on a security log whose coverage the row itself calls unverified, and ADR 0005's own rule says a row without an observable event is a wish.
findings.scenario: Ten sessions pass; nothing counts them; the operator reads a security log that does not list a ruleset update on a personal account; an agent in one project merges and tags through the API; the trigger never fires and the narrowing is never reconsidered.
findings.change: Give the row a producer: either a check (a session count the handoff reader derives from facts files per repo, or a date the operator writes in host state that doctor compares) or the plain statement that the trigger is a calendar date the operator sets; and record in ADR 0005 that rule 1 has one accepted exception and how exceptions are counted.
findings.cost: a decision by the operator and either one doctor row or one sentence

findings.defect: The doctor table measures every credential path (secrets argv, signing socket, sbx globals) except the GitHub token the sandbox holds, whose reach 05 5.4 and ADR 0008 call 'inferred from the account's rights, not measured' although a token's type and scopes are one API response header.
findings.scenario: The operator rotates the Keychain entry to a classic token with admin:org and workflow scopes by mistake; nothing on the host notices; every sandbox on the machine holds it.
findings.change: Add a doctor row, marked pre for a project that binds a github secret: run the bound argv, read the token's type from its prefix and its scopes from the API's x-oauth-scopes header (or the fine-grained token's repository list), fail when the reach exceeds the project's repositories or includes Administration; add the same reading as a block A probe so the ADR's 'inferred' becomes measured.
findings.cost: one doctor row that makes one network read outside the preflight's no-network rule (state the exception), one probe observation

findings.defect: The Context says 'the forwarded SSH agent holds the signing key and a separate GitHub authentication key', which 06 6.4 forbids for a romeu sandbox (RJ-204, exactly one key), and the record does not say which sandbox it measured, so the 05 5.4 rows and the deferred rows written from it describe the development sandbox as if it were the product.
findings.scenario: A secondary user (00 0.2) reads 05 5.4 and believes their product sandbox holds their whole GitHub account; the maintainer reads 06 6.4 and believes the one-key rule protects the sandbox they work in, where romeu does not run.
findings.change: Add a scope sentence to ADR 0008 Context and to the head of 05 5.4's last rows: the sandbox measured is the one the product is built in, not a romeu sandbox; for a romeu sandbox the token is the name@project binding (Q13) and the agent socket is the one-key socket (06 6.4); say which rows hold for which reader.
findings.cost: three sentences; no mechanism

findings.defect: 'Release signing' and ADR 0008 decision 6 fix a rule about 'the credential that signs release artifacts, held outside GitHub', but S1 lists only checksums.txt and keyless attestations, J1 step 2 verifies only those two, and 10 10.2 has no signing step, so the rule names a control that does not exist and that no task builds.
findings.scenario: The sandbox's token merges and pushes a v* tag (05 5.4); release.yml builds and attests; checksums match; a user runs the J1 commands and installs; the 'operator step' that was to sign never happened because nothing defined its artifact or its verification.
findings.change: Either add the artifact (a detached signature of checksums.txt by an operator-held key) to S1, its verification command to J1 step 2 and README, and the step to 10 10.2 and the plan; or supersede the sentence in 05 5.4 and ADR 0008 and say plainly that the only release trust is the attestation of a workflow the sandbox's token can trigger.
findings.cost: a decision; then either one operator step with a key to manage or two deletions

findings.defect: The workflow grammar admits permissions of read or none only, while 'Release and bootstrap' has release.yml create a release and attest (contents, id-token and attestations write) after running tools/ci all, the change's own tests, on each runner; the grammar cannot express the file, and nothing says the tests run in a job without the publishing credential (the deferred row on a separate job names ci.yml's judging steps only).
findings.scenario: release.yml is written with write permissions at the top; tools/ci workflows is widened to pass it; a test merged by the sandbox's token runs in the same job and token as tools/release publish and replaces the archive after checksums.txt is written.
findings.change: In 10 10.2, state that release.yml has two jobs, the tests and build with read permissions and the publish and attest job with write permissions and no step that runs code of the change; extend the grammar to admit write only in a job whose run lines are tools/release publish, verify and tools/ci dora --attach; add release.yml to the deferred row about a separate test job.
findings.cost: two sentences, one grammar rule, and T088's acceptance changes

findings.defect: The maintainer runs agent-authored code on the host by design: the pre-push hook runs the pushed branch's own tools/ci fast (12 12.4), and the maintainer block and blocks O3 and O6 run the hook and tools/ci on a host clone after 'reading the diff' (10 10.2, plan.md), yet 05 5.4 has no row for it and the review it rests on is one no ruleset requires.
findings.scenario: An agent's branch adds a test helper under tools/ci; the sandbox's token merges it; the maintainer later pushes probe results from a host clone and the hook runs main's tools/ci fast on the host with the maintainer's user and Keychain.
findings.change: Add a 05 5.4 row: 'the maintainer executes tools/ci and the pre-push hook on the host; their code is agent-authored and merged by a token the agent holds; the control is the maintainer's read of the diff and the ask-first list'; scope the sentence of 00 0.1 to romeu's runtime; name in 10 10.2 that the hook on a host clone runs from main only (git config core.hooksPath to a trusted checkout) or accept the gap by name.
findings.cost: one row, one scoping clause, one decision about where the host's hook code comes from

findings.defect: A12 measures ssh-add -L inside a sandbox only with SSH_AUTH_SOCK set to a one-key agent; the case every project without git-ssh-sign relies on, the variable unset in romeu's scrubbed env (04 4.1) with a workload that declares ssh-agent, is unmeasured, and B2 measures only the used case.
findings.scenario: sbx forwards the host's agent through its own socket path regardless of the invoking environment (as Docker Desktop does for containers); the operator's default agent, with its GitHub authentication key, is in every sandbox, and the scrubbed env was never a control.
findings.change: Add to A12 a second observation: with SSH_AUTH_SOCK unset for the sbx process and the workload's ssh-agent capability declared, ssh-add -L inside lists no key; add to B2 that a project without git-ssh-sign lists no key; make the A12 result settle Q19's 'what holds until then'.
findings.cost: two probe observations; a possible redesign of 04 4.1 if the answer is bad

findings.defect: 'Strict decoding (unknown keys are errors)' is the only parse rule for every format, and the strict subset grammar (no anchors, aliases, merge keys, includes) of 01 1.4 is stated for descriptors alone, while memory entry and handoff front matter (03 3.9, 03 3.10), heads.json and the TOML locks (07 7.5) are agent-authored and parsed on the host by yaml.v3 and BurntSushi/toml with no stated limits beyond the 1 MiB file cap, and the fuzz list of 10 10.1 does not name them.
findings.scenario: A memory entry's front matter holds nested aliases that expand far past the file's 1 MiB; romeu sync's List reads it and the host process exhausts memory before the allowlist check that would have passed the file.
findings.change: Move the strict subset grammar to 03's opening as the rule for every format romeu decodes from a mount or a repository, name the memory entry, handoff, heads.json and lock parsers, state a decoded-size bound, and add those decoders to the fuzz list of 10 10.1.
findings.cost: one paragraph moved and widened; four fuzz targets

findings.defect: Every field that becomes a file or an argv element on the host has a rule except kit args keys and values, which travel from the spec into sbxenv.yaml and into sbx's kit build, and the domain rule is stated for egress.extra only while lock-derived hosts and kit-declared domains (07 7.5) become arguments of sbx policy allow network.
findings.scenario: A personal kit arg of several kilobytes with newlines and a kit-declared domain with a trailing dot or a port pass validation, appear in the gate diff, and reach sbx's build and policy argv in a shape nobody tested.
findings.change: Add to 03 3.1 a row for kit args (key ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,31}$, value printable, length cap, no newline) and state that the domain rule applies to every domain source of 07 7.5.
findings.cost: two rows in rules.go and the generated schema

findings.defect: snapshot/heads.json (ref to SHA, created) is agent-written and read by romeu status and romeu pull, and it has no schema in 02 2.1, no section in 03 and no version field, against 03's rule that every format has all three.
findings.scenario: A heads.json with a ref name holding a terminal escape or a SHA field that is not hex reaches status output and pull's head comparison through an undefined decode.
findings.change: Add a 03 section and schemas/snapshot.v1.json for heads.json with version, ref-name and hex rules; list it in 02 2.1.
findings.cost: one schema and one short section

findings.defect: The host-settings rules (argv[0] absolute and exists, no shell strings) and I25 (no secret value written by romeu) do not forbid a secret value as an argv element, and 01 1.4 says the gate diff shows the argv behind each secret name, so a literal placed there is rendered into sbxenv.yaml, printed in the gate diff, visible in the sbx process list and stored by sbx's remembered host commands.
findings.scenario: An operator binds github@shop to [/bin/echo, ghp_...] to 'get going'; romeu renders it, the gate prints it, and it sits in a world-readable process list and in sbx settings.
findings.change: Add to 03 3.4 the rule that an argv is a command that fetches the value and never carries it, with a doctor row that fails an argv element matching the common token shapes (ghp_, gho_, github_pat_, a 40-hex string) and a note under I25 that this is why.
findings.cost: one rule, one doctor row with a small pattern table

findings.defect: The insteadOf paragraph names two cases (a rewrite to a refused protocol, a rewrite to another HTTPS host) and not the third, a rewrite to git://127.0.0.1, the one protocol gitsafe allows, which would make the sandbox daemon the origin for sync --from reachability and egress derivation; core.gitProxy is not in the neutralized -c list; and the I3 planted list omits both, while the doctor table reads only the global config and not a host clone's local one.
findings.scenario: A host clone's local config gains url.https://github.com/.insteadOf=git://127.0.0.1:<port>/ (trusted writers, so by mistake); the next sync reads specs the sandbox served as origin.
findings.change: Name the third case in 05 5.1 and refuse a rewrite whose target host is 127.0.0.1 for a URL that was not; add -c core.gitProxy= to the flags; add core.gitProxy and a local insteadOf to the I3 planted list; add a doctor row that reads each host clone's local config for url.*.insteadOf, core.hooksPath and include.*.
findings.cost: one flag, two test rows, one doctor row

findings.defect: The signing rule bounds the socket to one key equal to signingKey but no rule says that key must be registered on GitHub as a signing key only, and 'confirm-on-use where the agent supports it' (05 5.4) is not a rule the guide states or doctor can read.
findings.scenario: The operator registers one ed25519 key as both authentication and signing key; the forwarded one-key socket then authenticates the sandbox to every repository the key can reach, with no token involved, and signs any number of commits without a prompt.
findings.change: Add to 06 6.4 and the J1 guide that signingKey is registered on GitHub as a signing key and never as an authentication key, and that the key is added to the dedicated agent with ssh-add -c; add the first to the 05 5.4 row on Verified signatures.
findings.cost: two sentences and a guide step

findings.defect: The row 'GitHub rate limit' hands the project's github secret to mise as a download token without saying that today that secret is the operator's own account token (ADR 0008), so a reader of 07 sees a download credential where 05 5.4 sees administrator reach.
findings.scenario: A tool install over an aqua/github backend sends the operator's token to a redirect host the catalog marked upload: false; the row's reader did not know what the token could do.
findings.change: Add to 07 7.4 a pointer sentence: the github secret is the operator's own token until the narrowing row of the index fires (05 5.4), so this download path carries that reach.
findings.cost: one sentence

findings.defect: The Threat model defers two go run escapes 'until the hook next changes, or until the sandbox-token question (Q25) is decided', cites a plan row that no longer exists, and rests sabotage detection on 'the review's job'; Q25 is decided (ADR 0008), no review is required (05 5.4), and nothing records that the trigger fired.
findings.scenario: An agent's branch adds an untracked go.work in a parent directory on the maintainer's clone path or sets GOFLAGS=-overlay in a mise env the hook reads; the hook's tools/ci fast runs replaced code on the host; the deferral that was to reopen on Q25 never did.
findings.change: Add the two escapes as a row of the index's Deferred decisions with a trigger that exists (the next change to .githooks/pre-push, or the first host push after ADR 0008), or close them now by having the hook start tools/ci with GOWORK=off and GOFLAGS unset; add a Consequences line via a new record that the Q25 trigger fired on 2026-10-07.
findings.cost: one deferred row or two environment variables in a one-line hook; one superseding note

findings.defect: Rule 8 says 'the code-owner review and the merge are what an author cannot type', ADR 0002 rule 3 says a merge needs the full check list to pass, and ADR 0003 says the ruleset requires one approving review; all three are false since 2026-10-08 and ADR 0008 leaves them standing by pointer, although the standard's own mechanism is a superseding record.
findings.scenario: A new contributor reads ADR 0001 rule 8 and relies on a barrier that the measured ruleset does not have.
findings.change: Add to each of the three records a one-line Status note 'see ADR 0008 for what the review is worth' through a new superseding or amending record, as rule 7 allows, rather than leaving the sentences unqualified.
findings.cost: one short record and three status lines

findings.defect: Identity is the sandbox name plus the workspace path from sbx ls --json plus an open generation; a sandbox of the same name recreated outside romeu at the same path passes while romeu's open generation belongs to the one that was removed, and 13 13.5 says the ledger treats the name as the identity across a retire.
findings.scenario: The operator removes the sandbox by hand with sbx and recreates it with the same name and workspace; romeu run finds it present with the old open generation, skips preservation, and salvage later imports from a sandbox that never held the lost work.
findings.change: Record in the generation the sandbox id or creation time that A4 shows sbx ls --json reports, and make I26 compare it; if sbx reports none, say so in I26 and add the hand-recreated case to its E tests as a known pass.
findings.cost: one field if the data exists; one test row either way

findings.defect: Q25 is marked decided by ADR 0008 and stays in the Open questions table until T101, so the table's own rule (a question leaves when settled) is broken for the one question that records the widening, and the row duplicates 05 5.4 and ADR 0008.
findings.scenario: A reader counts open questions and finds the widening among them; two texts describe one decision and drift.
findings.change: Remove the Q25 row now and let sequences check that an ADR cites it, or state in the table head that a decided row waits for its removal task.
findings.cost: one row removed

findings.defect: The salvage manifest's bundles[].file, files[].path, worktrees[].path and embedded-repo path are agent-chosen and the text relies on os.Root alone; no rule says they are relative, cleaned, below the salvage dir and free of symlink components, and no bound says how many bytes romeu hashes for files[] (08 8.5 host half step 1).
findings.scenario: A manifest lists ten thousand files of 100 MiB each; romeu hashes them all on the host before deciding completeness; or a path with a symlink component is refused by os.Root with an error the reader cannot tell from corruption.
findings.change: Add to 03 3.11 the path rule (cleaned, relative, no .., no symlink component, below the salvage dir) and that the total bytes verified are bounded by salvage.capBytes, with the over-cap outcome named.
findings.cost: two sentences and one rule row

findings.defect: adopt records an existing sandbox as an open generation with an unknown recreate digest and the text does not say what it does not verify: the sandbox's actual mounts, kits and workload are never compared with the live sbxenv.yaml, and run then reattaches without re-provisioning (J3a).
findings.scenario: The operator adopts a hand-made sandbox that mounts $HOME read-write; romeu treats it as managed, runs julieta in it and salvages from it, and status reports nothing about the mount.
findings.change: Add to the adopt row of 04 4.2 and to 01 1.6 the sentence that adopt verifies name, workspace path and TTY only, and that status reports 'adopted: mounts and kits unverified' until a recreate.
findings.cost: two sentences and one status field

findings.defect: The row on running the change's tests in a separate job says an attack on the tools/ci process is 'out of its reach, and the review of the diff covers it', while 05 5.4 and 10 10.2 item a record that the ruleset requires no review, so the row's 'until then' names a control the same spec measures as absent.
findings.scenario: A reader of the deferred table believes the review stands between a test and the CI token until the first outside contributor; nothing does.
findings.change: Rewrite the 'until then' cell to say what holds: the token's read-only permissions in ci.yml and nothing else; and add release.yml to the trigger as in L2b-8.
findings.cost: one cell

findings.defect: Item d measured four tries and declined the one that matters most for the widening, a ruleset body change, so 'an agent can disable the ruleset' stays 'inferred, not measured' in 05 5.4 and ADR 0008 where a reversible try (change, read back, restore) was available in the same sitting.
findings.scenario: The inference is wrong in the other direction (GitHub refuses the edit for a token without a specific permission) and the spec carries a risk row and a deferral that a ten-second try would have removed; or it is right and the row says 'inferred' where 'measured' would close debate.
findings.change: Add a fifth try to item d, run at the next sitting: update the default-branch ruleset's enforcement to disabled and restore it, reading the body back each time; record the result in ADR 0008 by a new record and in 05 5.4.
findings.cost: one operator try and one record

findings.defect: Step 2 reads a spec from an unmerged branch head with sync --from <sha>, and 01 1.1 says config-repo merges are reviewed; on this path the gate 2 diff is the only review and the journey does not say so.
findings.scenario: The operator approves a gate for a branch spec expecting a later PR review to catch what the gate does not show (run pane steps), and the branch is never merged.

findings.defect: The plan's opening says 'the seven decision records under adr/' while the repository holds eight, and 'What v1 leaves out' says the Deferred decisions table has 28 rows while the index has 36 at 2cf36fa.
findings.scenario: A reader trusts the plan's counts and misses ADR 0008 and eight deferred rows, several of them the token rows this lens cares about.

findings.change: Make T088 depend on the spec change of L2b-8 and name the two-job shape in its acceptance.

postmortem: After v1.0.0 the product failed the way this lens sees it: not by a sandbox escape but by the host falling through doors the spec left open on purpose, with controls that were memories. (1) The maintainer's host fell through the development loop, not through romeu: the pre-push hook ran the pushed branch's tools/ci on the host (10 10.2, 12 12.4) after a diff read; the change had been merged by the sandbox's own token (ADR 0008); the review ADR 0007 calls 'the review's job' was required by no ruleset (05 5.4). Crosses 00 0.1, 05 5.4, 10 10.2, 12 12.4, ADR 0007, ADR 0008. (2) The one widening had no measured edge and no counter: the sandbox held the operator's token and a forwarded agent with an authentication key; the control was a human reading a log of unverified coverage; the triggers counted nothing; a prompt-injected agent merged through the API and pushed a v* tag; the attestation signed what the workflow built; users verified as J1 says and installed. Crosses index Deferred, 05 5.4, 09 J1, 10 10.2, ADR 0005 rule 1, ADR 0008. (3) The release signing credential held outside GitHub did not exist: 05 5.4 and ADR 0008 described it, S1 and J1 did not, no task built it. Crosses 05 5.4, S1, 09 J1, 10 10.2, ADR 0008. (4) A personal kit's install step ran where nobody had said it would: 06 6.1 said sbx builds kits and never said where; the gate showed the step; the operator read 00 0.1 as covering it. Crosses 00 0.1, 01 1.3, 01 1.4, 06 6.1, 11 11.1. (5) romeu believed julieta: 01 1.2 never listed julieta's stdout among agent output, so no cap, decode or validation was specified, fuzzed or probed. Crosses 01 1.2, 04 4.1, 04 4.2, 06 6.3, 10 10.1, 11 11.1. lens_critique: This lens defines success as 'everything an agent wrote reaches the host as data', and that definition is satisfiable while the product still hands the agent the operator's whole GitHub identity: the lens over-weights the parser attack (an alias bomb in a memory file) against the plain fact that the agent can already push, merge, tag and delete across the account with no exploit at all, which the spec names and accepts. It also mistakes a complete gate diff for a control: a diff that is 'never truncated' and shows ten thousand lines is read by nobody, and the lens counts it as success. And it treats the host as the macOS machine, when for this product the thing worth protecting is the operator's time and identity across host, sandbox and GitHub; a lens that only guards the wall between two of the three will pass a spec that loses the third. Finally, the lens is biased toward adding checks; the product's own principle says to count concepts, and several findings here would be better served by one decision (narrow the token now) than by five doctor rows.
missing_viewpoint: The platform engineer who knows what sbx and Docker Desktop actually do: where local kits build, how an agent socket is forwarded, whether kit lifecycle hooks are host commands, what sbx ls --json identifies a sandbox by. Most of this lens's unknowns are platform facts the spec defers to probes that do not ask them; no listed lens owns the platform's semantics (L15 'the ground that moves' is the closest, but names change, not knowledge). A close second is the owner of the GitHub account and its organization policy, who is the real holder of the blast radius ADR 0008 widens.
